queue.profile_line: 68-year-old Vietnamese-speaking man living in his vehicle, recovering from a small stroke with mild right-sided weakness and walking on his own with a rolling walker.

review.summary: 68-year-old man, unsheltered and living in his vehicle, being discharged after a small left MCA stroke with mild right-sided weakness. He is modified independent with a rolling walker. The discharge summary names a stroke with a neurological deficit, which IHH's outline lists as ineligible (NEU-X1). The packet is also missing MRSA and COVID swabs, vitals, and an H&P. Clopidogrel is on the discharge summary but not on the pharmacy medication reconciliation.
review.reason_for_hospital_stay: Stroke (small left MCA) with mild right-sided weakness.

findings.headline: Stroke with right-sided weakness
findings.explanation: The discharge summary documents a stroke with mild right-sided weakness and new walker use. The outline lists stroke syndrome with neurological residual/deficit as ineligible. The weakness is described as mild and improving, so the coordinator may want to confirm with the hospital whether any deficit remains at discharge.

evidence.quote: with stroke (small left MCA), mild right-sided weakness
Functional status. Modified independent; uses rolling walker.

findings.rule_text: Stroke syndrome with neurological residual/deficit (e.g. ambulatory difficulty, seizure)

findings.headline: ADLs not detailed
findings.explanation: The chart gives overall function as modified independent but does not describe individual ADLs.
findings.rule_text: Able to complete all Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) independently including personal hygiene

findings.headline: Hygiene/showering not documented
findings.explanation: No note says whether he can gather supplies, transfer to the shower and bathe on his own.
findings.rule_text: Patient must be able to complete personal hygiene independently. Benches are available for bathing so seated shower is acceptable. Patient must be able to gather all of their own bathing/showering supplies, transfer to shower area and perform shower/bath independently

conflicts.topic: Clopidogrel on discharge list but not in reconciliation
conflicts.explanation: The discharge summary lists clopidogrel 75 mg daily. The pharmacy reconciliation lists only acetaminophen, docusate and pantoprazole. The hospital needs to confirm whether the antiplatelet continues.

Pantoprazole | 40 mg PO daily | Yes

suggestion.why: The chart documents a stroke with mild right-sided weakness, which falls under NEU-X1 (stroke syndrome with neurological residual/deficit). If the hospital confirms the weakness has fully resolved, the coordinator could reconsider.

ask_hospital: Confirm whether right-sided weakness or any other neurological deficit persists at discharge
Is the rolling walker new since the stroke? What distance can he walk?

Negative MRSA swab and COVID swab within 24 hours of admission
Clarify whether clopidogrel is continued (discharge summary vs. med reconciliation)
PCP follow-up appointment within 7 days and neurology follow-up
Psych history, conservatorship/FSP status, isolation status, behavior concerns
